```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(reactable)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(crosstalk)
```

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

data <- read.csv("https://manctsui.github.io/datasets/timesData.csv")
reactable(data, searchable = T, defaultPageSize = 5)
```

### Problem 1A

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

num_universities_by_country <- data |>
  group_by(country) |>
  summarise(num_universities = n_distinct(university_name)) |>
  arrange(desc(num_universities)) |>
  head(3)

reactable(num_universities_by_country)
```

### Problem 1B

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

ggplot(num_universities_by_country, aes(x=country, y=num_universities)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity")
```

### Problem 2A

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

top_50_unis_2011 <- data |>
  filter(year == 2011, as.numeric(world_rank) <= 50) |>
  select(world_rank, university_name) |>
  arrange(as.numeric(world_rank))

reactable(top_50_unis_2011, searchable = T, defaultPageSize = 5)
```

### Problem 2B

When turning data into a `SharedData` object we want a key that is unique to each row of data. If this is talking about Problem 1A, using something like `rank` as a key is irrelevant, there is not regard to the ranking in the data set from problem 1A. However, if this is about problem 2A, then it is still not a great choice. `world_rank` has the possibility of being shared between two universities even in the same year, for example both the University of California, Irvine, and University of Science and Technology of China both share the `world_rank` of 49. There are 4 universities that share the `world_rank` of 43. `world_rank` does not function well as a unique identifier, but `university_name` would, and is a much better choice for the key.

### Problem 2C

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

sd_top_50_2011 <- SharedData$new(top_50_unis_2011, key = ~university_name)

filter_slider("rank_slider", "Rank", sd_top_50_2011, column = ~as.numeric(world_rank))
reactable(sd_top_50_2011, searchable = T, defaultPageSize = 5)
```

### Problem 3

```{r}
#| warning: FALSE

data_2016 <- data |>
  filter(year == 2016) |>
  mutate(num_students = parse_number(num_students))

sd_2016 <- SharedData$new(data_2016, key = ~university_name)

plot_ly(
  sd_2016,
  x = ~student_staff_ratio,
  y = ~num_students,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Number of Students by Student Staff Ratio",
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Student Staff Ratio",
      nticks = 8
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Number of Students",
      tickformat = ",",
      nticks = 8
    )
  )

plot_ly(
  sd_2016,
  x = ~student_staff_ratio,
  y = ~teaching,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Teaching Score by Student Staff Ratio",
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Student Staff Ratio",
      nticks = 8
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Teaching Score",
      tickformat = ",",
      nticks = 8
    )
  )

```
